messages:
maria: Heads-up: found an inconsistency in api-ref/generate.md between the cURL and Python examples for routing header. cURL uses \"X-Redwood-Route\" and python uses \"x-redwood-route\" and the python value says \"canary-region\" which isn't a valid option.

kevin: thanks. do we know which values runtime actually supports?

maria: I checked runtime config briefly; it looks like the accepted values are default, canary, eu.

sam: runtime accepts headers case-insensitively but we should document canonical casing (X-Redwood-Route). I'll confirm the allowed values.

olivia: if runtime is case-insensitive we can state that but still show canonical header name in examples. I'll update text to "Optional header to prefer a routing pool. Header name: X-Redwood-Route (case-insensitive). Accepted values: default, canary, eu."

sam: confirmed. Also the python snippet should use requests.post (the current snippet has a small copy-paste bug). Current snippet: ```python
headers = {"x-redwood-route": "canary-region", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
```
Change to: ```python
headers = {"X-Redwood-Route": "canary", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
```

kevin: lint in docs CI will also complain if codeblock language hint is missing. add ```python for that block.

maria: I'll add a brief migration note: \"Older examples used \"canary-region\"; use \"canary\" instead.\"

olivia: I'll update the docs PR with canonical header casing, the python snippet fix, language hint, and the migration note. Also add a one-line server behavior note about fallback routing.

kevin: server behavior: if X-Redwood-Route omitted, request routes to default pool; traces include route_suggestion: null. Use wording: "If X-Redwood-Route is omitted, requests are routed to the default pool and traces will contain route_suggestion: null."

sam: I'll push a quick companion PR to the sdk-snippets repo to ensure the example snippet in the SDK matches the docs and add a tiny test that asserts the header string appears in generated HTML.

docs-bot: linked PRs: docs https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/458 , sdk-snippets https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-snippets/pull/102 . Docs CI initially failed (lint: excerpt-check).

maria: lint failure was the missing language hint and the mismatch in header value. Once those are fixed re-run CI.

olivia: fixed the codeblock hint, corrected snippet, added migration note, and clarified header text. Pushed.

docs-bot: Docs CI: passing. sdk-snippets PR includes unit test and passes.

maria: thanks all. One last ask: can we add a tiny line in the generate.md examples showing explicit header example for curl and python side-by-side so it's obvious? e.g., curl: -H \"X-Redwood-Route: canary\" and python header dict example.

sam: good idea. I'll update the sdk-snippets PR to include both examples and run the tests.

kevin: once merged, we should add a quick changelog note under docs/CHANGELOG.md: "generate.md: standardized X-Redwood-Route header casing and corrected example values."

olivia: added changelog entry in the PR. merging now. :shipit:

maria: perfect, thanks everyone!
